key_insight: Higher substrate temperature delays splat solidification, enabling greater spreading and producing denser, harder plasma-sprayed NiCrAl–10 wt.% TiB2 coatings.
engineering_relevance: Substrate-temperature control offers a practical route to improve coating integrity on lightweight aluminum components.
method: Atmospheric plasma spraying onto 6061-T6 aluminum at 230, 330, and 430 °C.
Linked individual splat spreading and morphology to bulk coating microstructure.
Evaluated coating porosity, microhardness, and phase composition.
evidence_signal: From 230 to 430 °C, mean splat diameter on polished substrates rose from 47.82 to 57.54 μm, coating porosity fell from 1.48% to 0.55%, and microhardness increased from 317.7 to 336.3 HV0.1, while the dominant γ-Ni(Cr,Al) phase remained unchanged.
watch_item: Before implementation, assess whether substrate heating alters the temper or mechanical properties of the 6061-T6 aluminum; the abstract does not report this evaluation.
paper_title: From Splat Spreading to Coating Densification: Substrate Thermal Effects in Plasma-Sprayed NiCrAl-TiB2 Coatings
